Compaction._comment: Enabled by default with ADR 0020's evaluated host settings. Set Mode to Off (or Compaction__Mode=Off) to opt out. MeasureCompactionGainOnStoredRows deliberately remains false.

ContextWindow._comment: Host ceiling on every model's context window, in tokens. A model whose Pricing entry states a larger MaxContextTokens is clamped to this; a model with no window (Claude CLI, Codex, any Copilot id not listed under Pricing:Models) gets exactly this, so the Context panel shows a gauge and compaction has a window instead of skipping with capacity_unknown. 0 turns the cap off (unknown models then show 'Unknown window' and never compact). Override with ContextWindow__MaxTokens.

ElapsedTimeNotice._comment: Experimental. Once per IntervalSeconds of wall-clock time inside a run, the loop appends a hidden, persisted note telling the model how long it has been working on the current request. Set Enabled false (or ElapsedTimeNotice__Enabled=false) to turn it off.

SandboxGateway._comment: Sandbox egress policy. Network:Rules are keyed by rule id; match lists are COMMA-DELIMITED strings, not arrays, so an environment/user-secrets override replaces the whole list atomically. Rules are evaluated ascending by Priority, first match wins, and the default action is deny. A rule named after a managed rule (github, github-egress, ado, m365) replaces it, and `Enabled: false` removes it. AuthProviders are keyed by id and emitted on the wire as `cfg-<id>`: `headers` injects static request headers from this app's own auth webhook, `webhook` hands the gateway an EXTERNAL callback with its own secret. Never commit a real secret here — override with SandboxGateway__AuthProviders__<id>__... or user-secrets. See AuthProviderGuide.md.

partner-api._comment: Disabled example: an authenticated rule referencing the partner-headers provider below.

Pricing._comment: Public list prices (#682). Every entry is copied from the vendor page in `_source` on `EffectiveDate`; nothing here is a guess. The Copilot-served ids the sample runs on (gpt-6-*, gpt-5.6-*, gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4.5, claude-haiku-4.5) carry the vendor's own retail API price as a public-equivalent estimate, not what the subscription bills; OpenAI ids use OpenAI's page, never a reseller's. DeepSeek ids use DeepSeek's off-peak rate. Claude CLI and Codex defaults stay absent. Schema and citation list: docs/features/public-pricing-catalog.md.

gpt-5.6-sol._comment: Retail API list price, used as a public-equivalent estimate for the Copilot-served id. Standard tier; OpenAI marks this price promotional through at least 2026-11-21. Prompts over 272K input bill at 2x input / 1.5x output, which a usage record cannot show.

claude-haiku-4.5._comment: Keyed by the Copilot id (dotted); the Anthropic API ids are aliases.

gpt-6-astra._comment: OpenAI's own list price (standard tier), not a reseller's. Cache writes list at $12.50 (1.25x input) but are not priced here: the usage record carries cache writes only from Anthropic's fields. Prompts over 272K input bill at 2x input / 1.5x output, which a usage record cannot show.

gpt-6-sol._comment: OpenAI's own list price (standard tier). Cache writes list at $2.50 (1.25x input) but are not priced here: the usage record carries cache writes only from Anthropic's fields. Prompts over 272K input bill at 2x input / 1.5x output, which a usage record cannot show.

gpt-6-luna._comment: OpenAI's own list price (standard tier). Cache writes list at $0.125 (1.25x input) but are not priced here: the usage record carries cache writes only from Anthropic's fields. Prompts over 272K input bill at 2x input / 1.5x output, which a usage record cannot show.

gemini-3.8-flash._comment: Google's paid-tier list price, promotional through 2026-12-31; from 2027-01-01 it doubles to $1.50 input / $0.15 cached / $7.50 output, so re-verify then. Served over Copilot's Chat Completions, whose cached_tokens sit inside prompt_tokens, hence SubsetOfInput.

claude-fable-5-1._comment: Cache hits on Fable 5.1 are 0.025x input, not the usual 0.1x. The dotted alias is the Copilot-style spelling.

deepseek-v4-pro._comment: Off-peak rate (owner decision). DeepSeek bills double this at peak hours, which a usage record cannot show, so peak-hour runs read low. Served over DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible API, whose input_tokens EXCLUDES cache reads, hence Additive.

deepseek-flash._comment: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, off-peak rate (owner decision); peak-hour runs read low. deepseek-v4-flash is the retired name DeepSeek still accepts and bills at this price. Served over DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible API, whose input_tokens EXCLUDES cache reads, hence Additive.

SubAgentIntelligence._comment: Map tiers 0-6 to ordered model-id fallback arrays. This is NOT only the tier ladder: SubAgentModelResolver derives the sanctioned model-override allow-list (IsKnownModel) AND the id menu the Agent tool descriptor advertises from exactly these values. An empty ladder therefore also empties the allow-list, so every `model` override the parent LLM sends is rejected as 'unknown' — including real, in-catalog ids (gpt-5.6-luna, the model actually running, was rejected in production) — and the descriptor lists no ids, so the parent invents them ('gpt-5', 'gpt-5.2', 'sonnet'). A tier mapped to [] is now reported as MISCONFIGURED by SubAgentIntelligenceOptions.Load and dropped, so the 'Tiers is empty' diagnostic can actually fire. A deployment override (e.g. appsettings.Development.json) or a one-line edit here is all it takes to change a tier's model.
SubAgentIntelligence._tier_mapping_comment: OWNER-APPROVED MAPPING (2026-09-23): 0 -> gpt-6-luna high, 1 -> gpt-6-luna xhigh, 2 -> gemini-3.8-flash high, 3 -> gpt-6-sol medium (fallbacks gpt-5.6-terra high, then gemini-3.8-flash xhigh), 4 -> gpt-6-sol high, 5 -> gpt-6-sol xhigh, 6 -> gpt-6-astra high. A candidate written 'model:effort' runs at its own effort instead of the tier's.
SubAgentIntelligence._efforts_comment: Reasoning effort per tier (low, medium, high, extra-high or xhigh). It applies to whichever tier a spawn LANDS on after climbing, so a model always runs with its own tier's effort. A sub-agent's authored `effort` still wins; otherwise the tier effort is raised to the conversation effort floor when the floor is higher. The model's capability shaper may still lower an effort the model does not support. A tier with no entry carries no effort of its own. A candidate's own 'model:effort' wins over its tier's entry, so tiers whose every candidate names an effort need none here.

AgentCollaboration._comment: Hierarchy-wide agent collaboration (#244). With Enabled omitted (as here) the chat mode decides: the Workspace Agent runs WITH collaboration — peer messaging, a hierarchy roster, and transcript reads bounded by TranscriptVisibility (Ancestors | Open) — while Workflow Author and the ordinary modes keep the pre-#244 tool surface and nesting limits. Add "Enabled": true or false to override every mode in that direction. The limits below apply wherever collaboration is on; MaxDelegationDepth counts ordinary spawn hops from the root (0), and a workflow controller is a free hop.

AzureAd._comment: Entra app registration for interactive sign-in (P1 #301). ClientId EMPTY here on purpose: with no client id no JWT bearer handler is registered at all, the SPA renders without a sign-in gate, and the whole identity pipeline is inert. That is the state every development machine and every existing test runs in. TenantId 'organizations' admits any work or school directory but not personal Microsoft accounts; which tenant a user belongs to is discovered from their token's tid and resolved against the tenants table, never pinned here.

Identity._comment: Enforce is GLOBAL - one process-wide flag, not per tenant (this supersedes the per-tenant flag of #237). False means an unauthenticated /api request resolves to a development principal rather than being refused, which is what keeps every current call path working. Flipping it to true refuses anonymous /api requests for EVERYONE in this process. The operator secret guarding POST /api/admin/tenants is deliberately NOT here: it is read from the LMSTREAMING_IDENTITY_OPERATOR_SECRET environment variable, and while it is unset that route answers 503 rather than succeeding.

Audit._comment: IncludeUpn records the presented preferred_username on a REJECTED sign-in. Off by default: a rejected sign-in is exactly the case where that identifier belongs to someone who is by definition not our user.

M365._comment: EmailMcpServer Entra app (mcqdb tenant). Confidential web client; ClientSecret MUST come from env (Auth__M365__ClientSecret) — NEVER commit it. Kept in base settings (not just Development) so M365 auth + scopes apply in Production too. Callback at /auth/m365/callback.
